content.text:
Built and shipped. Final state: **Files** - `index.html` — static shell with the full element contract (`#note-form` with `#title`/`#body`/`#avatar` + submit, `#search`, `#results-line`, `#feed`), labelled fields and a formatting hint. - `src/main.ts` — state, feed rendering, search, selection, fragment sync. - `src/richtext.ts` — the rich-text renderer. - `src/storage.ts` — localStorage load/save, seeding from `fixtures.json`. - `src/hash.ts` — `#q=…¬e=…` parse/build. - `src/types.ts`, `src/style.css`, `src/fixtures.json`. - `dist/` — production build (2.1 kB HTML, 8.5 kB JS, 2.9 kB CSS; no dependencies added). **How the rich text works.** Bodies are escaped first, then only the allow-listed tags are re-introduced by pattern — `
` and ``, plus newlines as breaks. Because the only markup in the output is markup the renderer emitted, nothing the user typed can become a tag or an attribute: `` doesn't match the pattern and stays visible as text. Link and avatar URLs are resolved through the `URL` API and restricted to `http`/`https`/`mailto` (`data:image/…` also allowed for avatars, which the seed data uses). Titles render emphasis but not links — the title *is* the button that selects the note, so a nested anchor would be invalid HTML. **Verification.** Beyond `pnpm smoke` (OK) and a clean `tsc --noEmit`, I drove the built app in a headless browser against a 36-check script covering the whole contract: seed order, ``/``/`` actually rendering bold/italic/clickable, avatars only where given, case-insensitive filtering, `results for "…"`, `#q=douro¬e=5` round-tripping in both key orders, add-and-clear with id 7, persistence across reload, and 12 injection probes (script tags, `onerror`, event handlers on allowed tags, `javascript:` hrefs, entity- and tab-smuggled schemes, attribute break-out in both body and avatar, iframe/svg). All 36 pass: no script ran, no `on*` attribute exists in the feed, and only allow-listed tags appear. Two initial failures were bugs in my test — a regex matching escaped *text* that looks like an attribute, and `example.com` being unreachable in the sandbox — not in the app; I tightened both to inspect real DOM attributes instead. The check script was temporary and is removed. One judgment call worth flagging: search matches the *visible* text of a note, so a query like `href` won't match markup the user never sees. If the shared suite expects raw-source matching, that's the line to change (`matches()` in `src/main.ts:28`).
